findings.evidence: The author already omits [CompleteSpace X] on all fourteen neighbouring theorems (GraphStep.lean:76, 89, 120, 175, 191, 233, 239, 254, 260, 271, 279, 287, 294, 306, 317, 324, 331), showing it is unused there; the definitions carry it purely by Lean's automatic instance inclusion. Only l.341 `(weakDerivStepSubmodule …).isClosed.completeSpace_coe` needs completeness of the ambient product.
findings.fix: Prefix those definitions with `omit [CompleteSpace X] in` (or scope [CompleteSpace X] to a section containing only the instance), leaving it on the CompleteSpace instance alone. This also removes the need for w3pSubmodule (W3p.lean:75) to have `CompleteSpace (W2p …)` available merely to form the graph.
findings.issue: [CompleteSpace X] is used only by the CompleteSpace instance (l.339) but is auto-included in every definition: weakDerivStepSubmodule (l.169), WeakDerivStep (l.218), prevL (l.225), prev (l.230), weakFDerivL (l.245), weakFDeriv (l.250), mk (l.266), and the private defs at l.71/84/97/107. The graph submodule, its membership characterization, its projections and its constructor hold for any normed X.

findings.evidence: GraphStep.lean contains no `⟪ ⟫`/`inner`/`innerSL`. Its dependencies are already stated over a plain normed E: `HasWeakFDerivOn` (WeakDeriv.lean:233), `setIntegral_smul_eq_integral_smul` (l.346), `setIntegral_lineDeriv_smul_eq_integral_lineDeriv_smul` (l.355), all under `variable {E F} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]` (l.153). `memLp_testFunction`'s proof is `phi.continuous.memLp_of_hasCompactSupport phi.hasCompactSupport` (W1p.lean:205), which uses no inner product; W1p already uses `omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]` at l.388 and l.402.
findings.fix: State GraphStep over `[NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]`, which requires generalizing the three test-function helpers it consumes — memLp_testFunction, testFunctionLp, testFunctionLp_apply_ae (W1p.lean:202/209/214) — to `[NormedSpace ℝ E]` (either in place, matching the existing `omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]` idiom, or by moving them next to the test-function API in WeakDeriv.lean). W2p/W3p instantiations are unaffected since InnerProductSpace implies NormedSpace.
findings.issue: The order-independent step assumes [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] on the domain, but no declaration in the file uses inner-product structure; only W1p's Riesz gradient needs it. Every exported declaration of the new generic API is therefore restricted to inner-product domains without cause.

summary: The specialization duplication is fixed: W2p and W3p are now one-line derivations of the WeakDerivStep API, so I withdraw those findings. Two over-strong hypotheses remain on the new order-independent file: an unused [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] and [CompleteSpace X] on every definition.
